harm: A process exit during restored-file staging leaves a temporary file which prevents the same destination from resuming.
reproduction: Actual subprocess os._exit(91); failed before repair, passes after.
repair: Stage recovered bytes inside retained work-restore-evidence.

harm: A process exit during progress JSON replacement leaves a staging file outside the evidence area, blocking resumed restoration.
reproduction: Actual subprocess exit before second progress replacement; failed before repair.
repair: Stage restoration metadata and its recovery reference inside the same retained evidence area.

harm: Replaying a completed rollback deletes a later identical file recreated at the former destination; a later changed file instead causes a spurious failure.
reproduction: Both identical and changed post-rollback files fail the regression before repair.
repair: After checking the saved approved-plan binding, replay a terminal fully rolled-back journal without filesystem mutation.

harm: Crash between destination creation and publication of the first restore marker leaves ownership uncertain; same destination cannot currently be adopted automatically.
reproduction: Actual subprocess exit before first restore marker commit; same destination rejected unchanged; same saved run restores at alternative destination.
repair: Error now explicitly directs recovery of the same run at a new destination. Unreceipted contents are never adopted.

harm: Search/open currently reject every indexed source after any top-level scope change, even an unrelated added client folder.
reproduction: New unrelated client blocks selected-scope search and verified opening before repair.
repair: Allow exact unchanged selected scopes; keep global refresh requirement and source byte verification; return refresh flags.

harm: Folder intake uses hard-link publication and may fail on writable destinations lacking hard-link support.
reproduction: Subprocess tests force ENOTSUP and EXDEV during hardlink publication. Normal copy and actual os._exit(93) during fallback publication verify exact retry.
repair: Fallback to exclusive file creation on unsupported/cross-device links. Small sealed per-file publication records retain partial bytes separately before retry; completed/changed unrelated files remain protected. Evidence preservation copies and verifies before unlink, so it works across filesystems.

harm: Creation retry returns an empty import list after documents have been saved, misleading the caller about retained work.
reproduction: Reproduced in installed Vera 0.1.597 assessment; local regression fails before repair for healthy and changed retained inputs.
repair: Hydrate current validated imports and expose blocked-input/completeness information on creation responses.

harm: A destination created concurrently after restore preflight receives restoration metadata before unrelated-content rejection.
reproduction: Inject ordinary owner-private folder creation at mkdir; its directory gains unwanted restore files before repair.
repair: Exclusive destination mkdir for new restore requests; existing receipted requests retain resumability.

harm: ImportError in deferred reporting dependencies prevents finalization or hides committed completion/failure/cancellation.
reproduction: Five fault-injection cases fail before repair, existing OSError cases pass.
repair: Handle ImportError at review-report and terminal-report boundaries, returning unavailable/retry-pending independently of run status.

harm: Drive rollback trusted mutable journal source locations without binding them to the reviewed approved plan; altered journal data could move a file to an unrelated parent or name.
reproduction: Three regressions modify source parent, source name or approved-plan digest after apply. All fail before repair.
repair: Validate journal owner, storage root, approved digest, operation coverage and immutable file/source/target identities before loading a Drive gateway or mutating remote state.

harm: Completed Drive rollback replay claims remote changes and rewrites the journal although no move occurred.
reproduction: Repeated rollback fails nonmutation/count/receipt-preservation assertions before repair.
repair: Return a replay result with zero mutations for a fully rolled-back journal after approved-plan validation.

harm: Rebuilding a review package or changing persisted decisions after apply appears able to overwrite the plan/decisions needed to validate rollback. Review writers also lack the client-wide mutation lock used by apply/rollback.
reproduction: Prepare, save and compile calls after apply overwrite retained review evidence before repair. Three regressions now require unchanged output bytes and successful rollback of exact originals.
repair: Review writers share the client-wide apply/rollback lock and retain existing review artifacts once an apply journal exists.
followup_regression: Expanded MCP suite caught unsupported language creating a lock before rejection; validate explicitly supplied language before lock creation. Existing no-write regression now passes.

harm: Drive list pagination has no repeated-token detection or total bound, and recursive snapshot folder traversal is not bounded by its file limit. Repeated pages or very large empty-folder trees can monopolize work.
reproduction: Finite fake API test detects repeated request on same page token; 5000 empty child folders bypass file limit before repair. Both regressions fail before repair.
repair: Reject repeated pagination tokens as incomplete and bound folder traversal to 5000 including root; preserve ordinary file limit and report oversized roots explicitly.

harm: Archive page language rendering throws because model-data-link no longer exists.
reproduction: Headless browser observed Cannot set properties of null (setting href) in all five languages before repair.
repair: Remove the obsolete link assignment; the shared final model-data component owns its links.
verification: html-browser.json: five language URLs, desktop/mobile overflow checks, zero script errors; screenshots inspected with remote assets deliberately blocked.

harm: Optional local Gmail query planner omitted the Bcc participant term required by the documented connected workflow.
reproduction: Selected-client query regression fails before adding bcc for the same confirmed address.
repair: Include Bcc in the bounded exact-participant query; no mailbox calls or routing relaxation.

harm: A failed WhatsApp digit action reported composerEmpty=true without observing the state after that action; a lost reply could conceal a changed composer.
reproduction: Executable Node guard test simulates a lost digit reply and fails before repair.
repair: Stop with composerEmpty=null and cleanup=unverified; do not guess or erase unknown content.

harm: Unique endless Drive page tokens cause unbounded API requests; child lists accumulate before tree limits apply.
reproduction: Two regressions fail before repair after a fourth API request exceeds a configured three-request test boundary.
repair: Bound each folder listing to 100 pages and 10000 children; report incomplete listing without returning partial results. Complete final pages at the exact bounds remain accepted.

harm: Malformed Office XML aborts the whole refresh, preventing healthy documents from being indexed.
reproduction: Valid DOCX and XLSX containers with malformed document/workbook XML both raise uncaught XMLSyntaxError before repair.
repair: Isolate XML syntax failures as per-document extraction errors, retain original bytes, and continue indexing healthy files.

harm: Process exit before run.json publication leaves an invalid run directory, preventing retries and allocation of other jobs in the engagement.
reproduction: Actual subprocess os._exit(95) after context.json; retry fails with incomplete request identity before repair.
repair: Build complete job inputs and manifests in engagement-local run-preparation-evidence, then rename the complete directory into runs under the engagement lock. Preserve interrupted staging; do not delete a published run if post-publication loading fails.

harm: Missing selective_reporting dependency aborts finalization while importing the runtime, then again during metadata delivery even after sealing succeeds.
reproduction: Actual import failure injected via sys.modules; regression fails at import first, then at metadata_result after initial repair.
repair: Load routing lazily inside reporting operations, preserve its callable API for preview, and return the sealed outcome directly when reporting is unavailable.

harm: Nonfinite JSON numbers in one client manifest raise an uncaught canonicalization error and hide healthy clients during inventory.
reproduction: NaN, Infinity and -Infinity each fail before repair.
repair: Reject nonfinite values in the bounded JSON reader and translate invalid JSON into LedgerError for independent-record isolation.

harm: Missing reporting imports block output declaration preview and make report verification throw even when saved options request local-only handling.
reproduction: Preview and both local_only false/true verification cases fail with ModuleNotFoundError before repair.
repair: Keep preview output with a separate unavailable report status; defer receipt imports until after local-only handling and catch import failures in verification.

harm: Archive Organization review MCP selects VIRTUAL_ENV or system Python directly, unlike Studio Archive managed worker routing. Installed launch without VIRTUAL_ENV may select an incompatible or dependency-incomplete interpreter.
evidence: Read archive-organization/mcp/server.cjs pythonExecutable/callCli and vera/scripts/component_service.cjs; wrapper forwards environment without selecting Python. Existing MCP contract tests explicitly supply VIRTUAL_ENV.
next_step: Reproduce product-layout launch with an available managed runtime and an unsuitable bootstrap interpreter; fix routing if failure confirmed.
reproduction: Product-shaped test with managed Python available, no VIRTUAL_ENV and no Python on PATH failed with spawnSync python3 ENOENT.
repair: Probe available managed/PYTHON/virtualenv/PATH interpreters; packaged components delegate commands to the product managed_python_runtime.py launcher. Standalone source components retain direct CLI routing.
limitations: Launcher response is a bounded test stub; this proves executable discovery and command delegation, not installed package or Windows acceptance.

harm: Exact reopening of a completed reconciliation re-admits original sources before checking the retained job, so missing originals prevent access to otherwise valid retained results.
reproduction: Completed real synthetic producer run, deleted originals, forbid preflight/recalculation; retry failed in source preflight before repair.
repair: Resolve exact request identity and compare the retained request before admission. Verify sealed outputs before reopening completed/review-ready work, and preserve changed-mapping rejection.

harm: An incomplete report pair is rejected by shared professional-output closure, preventing downstream work solely because JSON or Markdown reporting output is missing.
reproduction: Both partial-pair cases failed before repair in archive_reporting_paths; same guard exists in JavaScript consumer.
repair: Keep surviving ordinary reserved sidecars separate from professional outputs using the owning run context, warn that reporting is incomplete, and retain foreign identity and unsafe-file rejection.
validation_gaps: Installed package, full release checks and fresh-chat acceptance remain pending.
validation: 12 focused boundary tests and 197 combined output-boundary/filesystem tests passed. Broader failures were corrected test fixtures: technical artifact was incorrectly treated as an accounting decision; missing measurements were expected without injecting a measurement failure.

harm: When publishing a review fails and restoration also fails, unconditional cleanup deletes both the reconstructed original and detached backup, losing the retained professional result.
reproduction: Inject EACCES for both candidate-to-output and recovery-to-output renames. Public transaction reports rollback failure but before repair no original backup survives.
repair: Remove recovery staging only after verified restoration; retain transaction and commit evidence when rollback fails.
validation: 13 output-boundary tests and 42 existing Report Builder/Vouching review-transaction regressions passed; Node syntax, Isort and diff whitespace checks passed.
validation_gaps: Automatic recovery after process termination and discoverable retry handling remain under review.

harm: A process exit after detaching canonical outputs leaves the normal output directory absent, although trusted backup and validated candidate survive in the commit directory. Resume behavior is not yet verified.
reproduction: Real Node process.exit(96) immediately after outputs-to-trusted-backup rename. Canonical output absent; original and candidate files retained. See outputs/studio-archive-hardening/review-process-exit.json.
repair: Persist output, host, parent-directory and commit-directory identity plus original/candidate byte-mode digests before detach. Retry atomically claims an abandoned commit, verifies retained bytes, restores the original and retains crash evidence separately. A parent rename retains identity; moved evidence from another parent, active owners or changed evidence are preserved without overwrite. Consumer preflight and path-based review loading invoke recovery first.
validation_gaps: Whole-transaction concurrent writers remain under review.
Package/release checks and fresh installed supported-host acceptance remain pending.
validation: Three real commit-exit phases, exit during recovery, changed backup, independent canonical output, live-owner rejection, renamed-parent recovery and foreign-parent rejection. Native Report Builder retry succeeds. Stable combined batch: 74 passed; embedded consumers: 57 passed; final boundary/native batch after parent-identity correction: 23 passed.

harm: The reporting failure recorder imports its storage dependency before its exception boundary, and projection isolation omits ImportError. Missing reporting dependencies can therefore hide an already committed result or interrupt a producer.
reproduction: Two regression cases failed with the injected ImportError: metadata delivery after collector failure with unavailable gap storage, and projection lookup with an unavailable collector binding.
repair: Move optional storage import inside the failure boundary and include ImportError in the shared reporting-only error set. Preserve unavailable status, measurement gap and whether the gap was saved. Canonical helper synchronized across all three products.
validation: 207 reporting/recovery/fault tests passed, followed by both targeted regressions after final synchronization.

harm: ImportError escapes uncached job lookup reporting retries, terminal recovery batches, receipt stamping and non-strict pending-proof retries. This can prevent saving valid work or stop healthy sibling retries.
reproduction: Four new cases failed with ImportError before repair; existing OSError recovery case remained passing.
repair: Handle missing reporting dependencies at the four specific boundaries, retain pending warnings/status, and continue independent work or retry entries without recalculation.
validation: 211 combined reporting/recovery/fault tests passed. Original report and professional-result bytes preserved.

harm: read_selection checks the source hash before parsing but not afterwards, allowing changed values to be returned with the admitted earlier hash when a file changes during extraction.
reproduction: Change a CSV between the admission hash and parser read; the new regression failed because no error was raised.
repair: Recheck source hash and symlink state after extraction, before returning data and provenance. Reject a changed source without overwriting it.
validation: 153 automatic-reporting, recovery and Agenzia delivery tests passed, including normal selected reads and changed-source rejection.

harm: The MCP reporting bridge cannot discover the managed Python interpreter when no PATH Python alias or active virtual environment exists; useful work is delivered with a measurement gap.
reproduction: Product-shaped real Node bridge with empty PATH and managed interpreter failed before repair.
repair: Discover the managed runtime and probe candidate interpreters before launching the recorder.
limitations: Stub recorder routing test on macOS; not installed report completeness or Windows acceptance.

harm: A valid large output declaration exceeds the host argv limit and fails with E2BIG before the Archive worker starts.
reproduction: 10,000 artifact declarations through a real Node subprocess failed with E2BIG on macOS.
repair: Send artifact JSON via standard input; retain run identity and command in argv, preserve direct CLI JSON option.
limitations: Transport regression checks all declarations intact; ordinary MCP lifecycle tests exercise the actual CLI and ledger. Not a 10,000-file finalization benchmark.

harm: Organization explanation page language application throws on an obsolete model-data-link element, before saving language and updating its URL.
reproduction: Real Chromium pageerror: Cannot set properties of null (setting href).
repair: Remove obsolete link assignment; shared function model-data component owns that section.
validation: All five language buttons update document, stored preference and URL; zero pageerrors and no desktop/mobile overflow. External assets blocked.

harm: A process exit while writing a job execution-runtime.json binding leaves partial authoritative JSON and prevents the next calculation/review attempt from resuming.
reproduction: Real subprocess exit 98 after writing one byte; retry failed with JSONDecodeError before repair.
repair: Stage and fsync complete binding under the existing execution catalog lock, then atomically replace the authoritative record. Existing job work is preserved. Canonical source synchronized to Vera, Clara and Lucia.
validation: 100 source/runtime/reconciliation cases passed; eight native-Windows cases skipped on macOS; one package test failed because vera-plugin.zip has not been built, and remains a release gate.

harm: Two overlapping review transactions can erase a successfully committed save: the older transaction detects a changed canonical tree and restores its stale image over the newer committed output.
reproduction: Two real Node processes: inner save reports saved true, outer fails and restores original output; regression fails before repair.
repair: Atomically publish unique per-output owner markers before capture or recovery. Any other live owner causes a retry response; terminated local owners permit recovery. No priority rule or mutable shared lock pathname permits overtaking. Claims cover recovery and the full transaction.
validation: 111 five-consumer transaction checks passed. Final 24-case boundary suite passed after root-path preflight and independent-output concurrency coverage. Earlier helper refresh omitted required insert_before argument; corrected before consumer checks.
limitations: Host-local ordinary-filesystem evidence. Foreign-host ownership is retained and explicitly rejected; simultaneous cloud-sync/network-host acceptance remains unproved.

harm: Organization page and skill claim Drive moves preserve permissions, although moving to another parent re-evaluates inherited access.
evidence: google_drive.py move_file updates addParents/removeParents; Google official manage-sharing guide states inherited permissions are re-evaluated on move.
repair: Correct all five page translations and Italian fallback; retain ID/link statement and explain destination-access boundary at the existing apply authorization.
limitations: No live Drive permission acceptance performed; no automatic access-equivalence check added or claimed.

harm: Failed client registration recursively deleted the newly visible client folder, including professional files added by another process during registration.
reproduction: Inject a registry write failure after adding a document to the visible destination; the document was missing after the failed operation.
repair: Preserve the visible folder and portable manifest; return an explicit incomplete-registration error with the retained path and existing-folder recovery instruction.
validation: 103 creation, fault-isolation, adoption and concurrency cases passed. The regression verifies preserved document bytes and reopening by the retained portable client identity. Updated the older committed-run interruption fixture to exit after atomic publication rather than during staging.

harm: Local organization evidence could change during extraction yet be returned as revalidated against the earlier snapshot.
reproduction: Change the selected text file inside extraction; before repair the public open call returned successfully instead of rejecting the stale citation.
repair: Resolve the selected path again and compare its current SHA-256 with the snapshot after extraction, before returning text.
validation: 38 customer-folder ledger tests passed, including ordinary local opening, changed local source rejection and simulated Drive revalidation.

harm: Unavailable checkpoint or navigation imports could obscure an already published prepared run. Missing input-repair code also rejected intact execution copies before ordinary receipt verification.
reproduction: Inject ImportError for vera_assurance.recovery or readable_archive; preparation raised instead of returning the committed run. Broader checks exposed the earlier load_run import boundary too.
repair: Return unavailable checkpoint/navigation outcomes, preserve ledger recovery results with navigation issues, and continue exact sealed-input verification when the optional repair module cannot load. Changed inputs still fail validation.
validation: 106 work-recovery, creation-recovery and fault-isolation cases passed. Initial narrower repair still failed at load_run; repaired that observed boundary and reran all three suites successfully.

harm: Local and Drive evidence reads could clip the final fragment without returning the open_text_truncated limitation. Separators were also outside the declared text budget.
reproduction: Public local and simulated Drive opens with an eight-character budget returned clipped text with no truncation indication; both regressions failed before repair.
repair: Use one bounded extraction projection for local and Drive evidence, include separators in its character budget, and compare full evidence length with returned length.
validation: 42 customer-folder tests passed, including clipped and complete reads on both routes. Drive uses a simulated gateway; no live Drive acceptance claimed.

harm: Incident failure reporting itself crashed with AttributeError when retained state was valid JSON but not an object.
reproduction: Twelve cases across Vera, Clara and Lucia: null, array, string and boolean state; all raised AttributeError before repair.
repair: Validate the state object before migration; preserve damaged bytes and return the existing local-state-unavailable result. Canonical runtime synchronized to all three products.
validation: 134 operational-incident and integrity-reporting tests passed. Synchronization check, Isort and three-module Mypy passed. This validates the reproduced top-level corruption case, not arbitrary nested-schema damage.

harm: Search explanation claimed exact phrases across full text and every supported file, although queries OR individual terms and extraction/discovery report format, access and size limits. Unused privacy translations duplicated the shared renderer source.
evidence: archive_core._fts_query, bounded extractors and scan issue reporting; both HTML files have no model.* data-i18n consumers and function-model-data.js fetches its own governed contracts.
repair: Clarify indexed-term search and extraction/discovery limits in all five languages and Italian fallback. Remove unused modelDataCopy blocks from both pages; keep the shared governed privacy renderer.
validation: Twenty Chromium checks passed across both pages, five language buttons and desktop/mobile widths: no overflow or pageerrors; visible last privacy section, language state and URL verified. External resources blocked. Architecture suite has 28 passing cases and one pre-existing missing navigation mapping for an unrelated integration page; remains a release gate.

harm: A missing post-commit metadata delivery import raised after finalization or completion had already saved the professional state.
reproduction: Both public finalization and completion regressions failed with ImportError after their durable state transition.
repair: Centralize guarded metadata delivery; retain a separate pending-reporting sidecar and return committed lifecycle/output results.
validation: 77 automatic-reporting and reporting-recovery cases passed, including ready-for-review/completed outcomes, retained output bytes and visible reporting failure.

harm: Report verification unexpectedly retried reporting when its private run binding was absent, violating its read-only contract and potentially modifying report evidence before verification.
reproduction: Network-failure, foreign-report and changed-report tests each failed when forced through portable-ID lookup because retry_reporting was invoked.
repair: Disable reporting retry specifically for report verification; ordinary operation retry behavior remains.
validation: 77 combined reporting cases passed; verification tests now cover both retained-binding and fallback lookup and assert unchanged files.

harm: Vouching private-file validation and rendering read canonical JSON before restoring an interrupted output transaction, hiding the retained review after a real process exit.
reproduction: Four public MCP cases exited the writer with code 96 immediately after canonical output detach. Both tools returned missing-path errors for explicit intake/review paths and review-path-only input.
repair: Invoke the existing verified output recovery before explicit private JSON reads, retaining its ownership, integrity and live-writer checks.
validation: All 38 selected Vouching tests passed, including all four real-process-exit/private-path regressions, read-only assurance replay, transaction faults and unsafe internal entries. Black/Isort across 50 changed Python files, changed JavaScript syntax and diff whitespace checks passed.

harm: An edit arriving after a pending intake file was copied to recovery storage but before its original path was unlinked was lost.
reproduction: Public folder-intake regression injects an edit at retirement after an interrupted copy; neither canonical tree nor recovery evidence contained those bytes before repair.
repair: Atomically move the actual partial entry into private recovery evidence, then validate that retained file. Do not delete a separately verified source after copying it.
validation: 25 intake/concurrency cases passed. Original source and concurrent edit bytes retained. Isort and Mypy passed.
